analysis: Examined three small changes. (1) ModelAutopilotSnapshot+Decoding.swift (head 33-39, 43-58): adds optional decoding of capabilities, adoptedModels, heldModels, busyReasons, busyReason, busySinceMs, transitionStalls, plus required-field decoders for ModelAutopilotHold and ModelAutopilotTransitionStall. This uses the same scoped snake_case/camelCase projection as existing code. The new fields carry model IDs and timing/status only, with no keys, prompts, or authorization. Decoding is local, from the daemon state file or wire snapshot, and optional fields are tolerant of older producers. A malformed present field throws, which is fail-closed. No new trust boundary or secret exposure is evident. (2) ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift: capacityRefreshTick (head 61-62) now calls superviseTransitions() synchronously before the rebuild, and its implementation is not supplied. Head 172-175 subtracts autopilotHeldWeightBytes() from the reclaimable MLX figure, saturated by min(mlxUsed, ...) so there is no underflow. This reduces advertised free_for_load_gb and so makes capacity reporting more conservative, not less. It does not touch attestation, App Attest authorization, encryption, or the prefix cache, so no T-041 or TB-011 interaction. Remaining uncertainty: the implementations of autopilotHeldWeightBytes() and superviseTransitions() are not in this batch. Whether superviseTransitions can unload or evict models, or can block the actor, is unverified. The same applies to whether the provider-controlled held-model data reaches the coordinator in a way that affects routing. A malicious provider already controls its own self-reported capacity under the existing threat model, so this is not a regression. (3) ProviderLoop+EngineV2.swift head 305: adds a wrapping generation counter increment when the reslice gate is acquired. This is a benign availability/consistency primitive. How it is consumed is not visible, so a next pass should check that consumers compare it correctly. No concrete security regression identified.
